correctness.rationale: The Paley-graph three-value adjacency spectrum follows from its strongly regular identity (or quadratic Gauss sums). For nonsquare q the two differences are Q-independent, so continuous Kronecker–Weyl equidistribution makes the time average equal to a uniform torus integral. Dirichlet circular spacings yield C3 exactly. For square q, a periodic integral yields Rk; the explicit q=9 and q=49 evaluations use exact trigonometric interval partitions. The standalone rational interval verifier certifies R3<C3<R1; finite-field and quadrature checks are ancillary.

value.rationale: The newly proposed unitary-separation heuristic can be constant across all nonsquare Paley orders even as graph size changes, yet square orders give deviations in both directions. The q=49 exact cyclotomic value is smaller than the non-square universal law while q=9 is larger. This structurally motivated finite/infinite classification is useful for assessing when a graph-topology spectral heuristic is sensitive to number-theoretic resonance, independently of any unproven algorithmic-success claim.
